From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement recap & next steps — PO vs credit card

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to hear how FinOpsCo is thinking about inference spend and vendor onboarding. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can loop in AP and Procurement: 

1) Current situation
- You have an internal policy that prefers POs for any vendor spend above $5k/month.
- Short-term pilot order volume is expected to be ~$7k/month if we move forward.

2) Commercial path options we discussed
- Option A: Standard PO + net terms (Procurement issues PO, legal signs SOW) — longer onboarding (2-4 weeks typical).
- Option B: Charge via corporate card for initial pilot while vendor onboarding completes — faster (days) but may be blocked by AP policy.
- Option C: Purchase via cloud marketplace (if available) which can speed purchasing and avoid some vendor onboarding steps.

3) Action items / asks
- Can you confirm whether AP will accept a marketplace vendor (AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace) as an alternative to a direct vendor PO?
- If marketplace isn't an option, can you introduce the AP contact (or share the vendor onboarding form) so we can start the paperwork?
- Attached: Redwood_Vendor_Packet.pdf (includes W-9, standard SOW template, SOC2 summary).

I can loop in our Finance/Legal leads if needed — cc'd Lauren here. If PO is the required path, we’ll prioritize completing the vendor packet and SOW to remove blockers. If card is possible for the pilot, we can start work immediately and convert to PO later.

Proposed next meeting: 30-min sync with AP + your procurement lead — are you available Wed or Thu this week?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Packet.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@finopsco.com>

Cc: AP Team <ap@finopsco.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement recap & next steps — PO vs credit card

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from AP: 

- Our AP policy requires a PO for any vendor relationship expected to exceed $5k/mo. The pilot you outlined would fall into that bucket, so we typically request the vendor be onboarded first.
- We can accept marketplace purchases in some cases, but AP requires marketplace vendor details and proof that invoicing and tax treatment are equivalent. Not all marketplaces meet our procurement controls.

I'm attaching our vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and the AP intake checklist — please complete those and we'll start the vendor setup. If you'd like to do a short pilot on card to accelerate, we'd need explicit approval from our procurement director; it's not the default.

Would appreciate you filling out the onboarding form and returning it. Once AP has that plus a W-9 and SOW, we can issue a PO (typical turnaround 5-10 business days after complete packet).

Best,
Sam Carter
Head of Cloud Finance | FinOpsCo
[Attachment: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (PDF, 45 KB)]
